# Input templates

## Relative-value quotes (`rv-quotes.template.xlsx`)

Task RV-1, 24 October 2026. CP-3 (`relative_value`) uses market evidence only from pack
sources that the CP-0 review classes `third_party`. In your own environment you supply that
evidence as an XLSX workbook with one sheet, `rv_quotes`, one quote per row. This template
shows the layout. Its six rows are a **synthetic example for a fictional issuer, not market
data**: replace every row. The `README` sheet in the workbook says the same.

The workbook is generated by `scripts/build_templates.py`
(`uv run python scripts/build_templates.py`), so the same rows always produce the same bytes.
`tests/product/test_inputs_rv_quotes.py` fails if the committed file and the script's output
differ. Edit the script, never the binary.

### Columns

Row 1 must be exactly these thirteen headers, from A1 to M1, in this order, with nothing after
M1. Each row from row 2 down is one quote. Blank rows are skipped.

| Column | Header | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `provider` | Required. The dealer, broker or pricing service that supplied the quote. It must not be the issuer's own name (compared without case or extra spaces): a quote the issuer supplies is not third-party evidence. |
| B | `as_of` | Required. Quote date as text `YYYY-MM-DD`, and a real calendar date. The template formats this column as Text. A date Excel has turned into a serial number (such as `46295`) is rejected. |
| C | `issuer` | Required. The issuer's name. |
| D | `facility_id` | Required. The facility's id, using only letters, digits, `-` and `_` (for example `TLB-2030`). Where you know it, use the id from the CP-1 Debt Facility Register (T4.18) so a reader can match the row. CP-3 does not join on this column. |
| E | `instrument` | Required. A plain description of the instrument. |
| F | `quote_kind` | Required. `observed` (a traded or firm level) or `indicative_talk` (talk, not a level). Lower case. Leave out rows without a quote: CP-3 records missing evidence itself. |
| G | `price` | Level. |
| H | `yield_pct` | Level, in percent (`7.10` means 7.10%). |
| I | `spread_bps` | Level, in basis points. |
| J | `bid` | Level. |
| K | `ask` | Level. When `bid` and `ask` are both present, `bid` must not be above `ask`. |
| L | `currency` | Required. A three-letter upper-case ISO 4217 code, such as `USD`. |
| M | `note` | Optional free text. |

Each row needs at least one level (`price`, `yield_pct`, `spread_bps`, `bid` or `ask`). Every
level must be a plain number. The validator reads each value as a decimal from the cell's
stored text, never as a binary float. No two rows may share the same `facility_id`, `as_of`,
`provider` and `quote_kind`. Enter values, not formulas: `prepare` freezes the stored values
and never recalculates. Hidden rows, columns and sheets are read like any others, and the pack
marks their cells hidden.

### Check the file

```
deploy-vii validate-input rv path/to/quotes.xlsx          # one line per issue, then a summary
deploy-vii validate-input rv path/to/quotes.xlsx --json   # the report as JSON
```

The command exits 0 when the file passes and 1 otherwise. A passing file ends `OK: <n> rows`;
a failing one prints one line per issue, then `FAILED: <k> issues`. Each issue reads
`<file>:<sheet>!<cell>: <problem> — fix: <fix>`, for example:

```
quotes.xlsx:rv_quotes!L2: currency 'usd' is not a three-letter ISO 4217 code — fix: enter the three-letter upper-case ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD
```

The validator reads the workbook through the same extraction `prepare` uses
(`preparation.xlsx_content`), so it checks exactly the stored values the pack will freeze.
These are the fixes it can print:

| Finding | Fix printed |
| --- | --- |
| `provider` empty | enter the dealer, broker or pricing service that supplied the quote |
| `provider` is the issuer | name the third party that supplied the quote, or leave the issuer's own levels out of this sheet |
| `as_of` empty, not an ISO date, or an Excel date serial | enter the quote date as text YYYY-MM-DD (format the column as Text so Excel keeps it) |
| `issuer` empty | enter the issuer's name |
| `facility_id` empty or with other characters | enter the facility's id using letters, digits, - and _ only, e.g. TLB-2030 |
| `instrument` empty | describe the instrument, e.g. Term Loan B due 2030 |
| `quote_kind` empty or not one of the two kinds | enter observed or indicative_talk; leave out rows without a quote |
| `currency` empty or not three upper-case letters | enter the three-letter upper-case ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD |
| A level that is not a plain number | enter a plain number: digits, an optional sign and one decimal point (no %, units, spaces or thousands separators) |
| No level in the row | enter at least one of price, yield_pct, spread_bps, bid or ask |
| `bid` above `ask` | check the quote: bid must not exceed ask |
| Duplicate `facility_id`, `as_of`, `provider`, `quote_kind` | keep one row per facility_id, as_of, provider and quote_kind, or correct the repeated value |
| A cell holds a formula | replace the formula with its value (Paste Special, Values) |
| Header row not the template's (missing, extra or out of order) | set row 1 to exactly: provider, as_of, issuer, facility_id, instrument, quote_kind, price, yield_pct, spread_bps, bid, ask, currency, note (A1 to M1, nothing after M1) |
| Header but no quote rows | add one row per quote, starting in row 2 |
| Sheet `rv_quotes` empty | copy the header row from docs/templates/rv-quotes.template.xlsx and add one row per quote |
| No sheet `rv_quotes` | name the quote sheet rv_quotes, as in docs/templates/rv-quotes.template.xlsx |
| Not an OOXML workbook (for example CSV or legacy `.xls`), or too large to prepare | save the file as an Excel Workbook (.xlsx) and validate again |
| File cannot be read | check the path and that the file is readable |

If the header is wrong, the validator reports only the header: it does not check rows against
a layout it cannot trust.

### How the file reaches CP-3

1. **Pack.** List the workbook as one source in your `prepare` request, with `media_type`
   `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`:

   ```json
   {"source_id": "rv-quotes", "path": "rv-quotes.xlsx",
    "media_type": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"}
   ```

   `prepare` freezes one span per stored cell, with locator `sheet:rv_quotes!<cell>`
   (`sheet:rv_quotes!A1` holds `provider`). It stores the raw values and evaluates no formulas.
2. **CP-0.** The CP-0 reviewer classes the source's authority. The `provider` column is what
   the reviewer reads to decide `third_party`. Python never sets the authority: if the
   reviewer classes the sheet anything else, CP-3 does not see it.
3. **CP-3.** For a source CP-0 classes `third_party`, each `observed` or `indicative_talk`
   market-evidence row quotes text from one cell verbatim, by its `sheet:rv_quotes`
   locator. CP-3's rules are unchanged: talk is never worded as a level, and with no usable
   evidence the preference is Insufficient Information.

Keep real quote files out of Git. They belong in your environment's pack root, not in this
repository.
